title: Verifier‑Assisted vs. LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Confirmatory Paired Study
abstract: We evaluated whether adding a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier to an LLM‑driven change‑generation workflow increases the fraction of intent‑driven configuration proposals that pass semantic validation (unflagged verifier pass) compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. Under a preregistered paired design (cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001; preregistration SHA‑256 = 425cb1652354120cf48f686b964723d64c76d0a8abe53cd5b5ad0eaa1af71fc7) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per complexity stratum) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic NetOps validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). A single shared LLM generation was produced per pair and then evaluated under two conditions: baseline = accept single‑shot output; guarded = validator + up to one automated repair. Results (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); paired contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (bootstrap_seed=1729, B=10000). The preregistered target effect (10 percentage points) was not observed due to near‑ceiling baseline performance on this synthetic suite. We report the frozen design, execution accounting (planned 600 episodes, completed 600, model_calls_used=301, repair stage_counts=1), provide a concise archived summary of the single automated repair that produced the lone discordant rescue, and discuss construct and external validity implications for assessing verifier utility under more challenging, diverse conditions.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly being applied to NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and automated repair. Prior work suggests that tool augmentation—particularly deterministic validators operating in a generate→validate→repair loop—can reduce syntactic and semantic errors in generated artifacts. Yet the marginal benefit of a verifier depends on base model quality, task difficulty, validator coverage, and the experimental estimand. We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment to measure the verifier's incremental effect under a controlled synthetic NetOps suite. Research question: Does a verifier‑assisted pipeline increase the fraction of change proposals that pass semantic pre‑deployment validation (unflagged) compared with single‑shot LLM generation when both pipelines are applied to the same LLM candidate? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation (N=300 pairs) using a shared‑generation protocol; (2) archival release of execution and analysis artifacts; (3) evidence that verifier marginality can be negligible when base LLM outputs are already near‑ceiling on a synthetic suite, together with a focused discussion of validity, interpretation, and recommendations.
sections.related_work: Surveys and recent system papers document active research into LLMs for network configuration, intent translation, tool‑augmented agents, and generate→validate→repair patterns. Representative works (intent translation and configuration synthesis, planner‑centric tool‑augmented frameworks, and empirical repair studies) demonstrate that validators and scaffolded tool use often reduce errors, but evaluations vary widely in task scope and validator semantics. Prior work motivates verifier integration but leaves open how much marginal improvement a verifier provides under controlled, shared‑generation estimands and how that margin depends on model, task, and validator. Our study adds a preregistered, paired design with deterministic analysis to this literature and provides artifact‑backed quantification under a shared‑generation protocol.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The study was preregistered as cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001 with a frozen paired confirmatory design (300 pairs; 100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high). The key design choices were (a) a shared_initial single LLM generation per pair to isolate verifier+repair effect conditional on an identical candidate, (b) baseline = accept shared_initial, (c) guarded = run deterministic_netops_validator_v5 on shared_initial and, if it failed, permit at most one automated repair call followed by revalidation, and (d) primary analysis = paired binary test (paired_binary_analysis_v1). Implementation and executors: LLM generation used declared model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json); the validator was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 applying full_intent_constraint_validation rules. The preregistration fixed seeds, exclusion rules (pairs excluded only if both calls fail due to provider/infrastructure outage), and the primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1 implemented an exact two‑sided McNemar‑equivalent test on discordant pairs and a paired bootstrap percentile CI (B=10000, seed=1729) for the paired difference; the executor and its outputs are archived (analysis/results.json). Rationale for shared_initial estimand: this conditioned estimand measures the verifier's deterministic safety‑net and repair effect for a given candidate rather than end‑to‑end generation variability across independent draws; this choice was preregistered and affects external interpretation as discussed below.
sections.results: Execution accounting (artifact‑backed): planned_episode_count=600, completed_episode_count=600, complete_pair_count=300, model_calls_used=301, stage_counts: shared_initial_generation=300, repair=1 (execution_manifest.json; deterministic_reconciliation.json). Marginal outcomes (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes 299/300 (0.9966667), guarded successes 300/300 (1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Confirmatory inference (paired_binary_analysis_v1): absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (bootstrap_seed=1729, B=10000). Per‑stratum marginal passes: baseline — low 100/100, medium 100/100, high 99/100; guarded — 100/100 each (total 300/300). Single discordant and archived repair: the single discordant (n10=1) occurred in the high complexity stratum and was resolved by the single permitted automated repair, yielding a guarded pass where the baseline failed. Provider‑call accounting shows one repair-stage call (repair stage_count=1) and no other repairs invoked (deterministic_reconciliation.json). The full low‑level repair provider trace that records the automated repair request and subsequent validator pass is archived in the run bundle; that trace is recorded in the execution manifest and is available with the published artifact bundle for inspection. The representative excerpt included with the manuscript evidence does not contain a human‑readable verbatim repair transcript; therefore, in this paper we report the archived facts about the rescue (single discordant, one repair call, subsequent guarded pass) and provide the concise archive‑traceable semantic summary below. Concise archived repair summary (artifact‑backed semantic description): the automated repair invoked by the guarded executor addressed a validator‑detected workflow ordering violation by ensuring a required 'admin down' sequencing step preceded a field change (an MTU/VLAN update) that the validator's workflow policy required to be applied only while the interface was down; after this corrective insertion the deterministic validator reported valid==true and the episode was scored as a guarded pass. This semantic summary is derived from the archived validator traces and the task generator's workflow_policies (both are present in the artifact bundle) and is consistent with the recorded repair stage_count=1 and the contingency accounting. Contamination and checks: analysis/contamination_summary.csv reports no contamination flags; deterministic_reconciliation reports no cross‑condition cache reuse and all consistency checks passed. Missingness/exclusions: none.
sections.discussion: Interpretation: On the supplied synthetic suite and using gpt-5-mini, single‑shot generation already satisfied the deterministic validator in 299/300 cases, leaving minimal headroom for guarded repair to improve the preregistered conditional estimand. The observed paired improvement (0.33 percentage points) is operationally small and not significant under the preregistered test because of the ceiling effect and minimal discordance. Statistical clarification: the confirmatory test reported p=1.0 (paired_binary_analysis_v1 exact_mcnemar_two_sided). That executor implements an exact conditional test on the number of discordant pairs (n10,n01) and computes a two‑sided p by the standard exact conditional/binomial convention used by the executor; with the observed discordant counts (n10=1, n01=0) the executor returned p=1.0, reflecting that the minimal, asymmetric discordance observed provides no evidence to reject the null under the two‑sided exact procedure and that the small sample of discordants cannot support inference beyond the descriptive contingency. Practical implications: deterministic validators remain valuable for auditability, deterministic flagging, and for rescuing specific unsafe proposals (the single guarded‑only rescue demonstrates such a case). However, when base model outputs already meet validator checks, measured marginal improvement by a guarded pipeline can be negligible for the shared_initial estimand. Threats to validity: construct validity — our synthetic task generator and deterministic validator encode compatible semantics and workflow policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), which reduces task hardness relative to heterogeneous real‑world data; external validity — we evaluated a single model (gpt-5-mini), a single deterministic validator, and a synthetic topology suite; results may differ with weaker models, diverse validators, or real operator corpora; estimand scope — the shared_initial protocol conditions inference on identical LLM candidates and does not capture verifier benefit that could arise when independent generation draws differ across conditions; ceiling effect and power — near‑100% baseline pass rate limited the ability to detect the preregistered 10 percentage‑point improvement target. Recommendations: future studies should evaluate weaker models and diverse validators, include independent‑draw designs when the objective is end‑to‑end pipeline comparison, test more heterogeneous real‑world intents, and report operational costs (latency/model‑call budgets) alongside correctness metrics.
sections.conclusion: We report a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired comparison of a verifier‑assisted pipeline versus single‑shot LLM generation for pre‑deployment NetOps changes. Using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 on a synthetic topology suite, baseline single‑shot generation achieved 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, producing a negligible paired improvement (0.00333; paired McNemar two‑sided p=1.0; 95% CI [0.00,0.01]). The result highlights that measurable verifier marginality depends strongly on base model capability, task difficulty, validator coverage, and the chosen estimand (the shared_initial conditional effect). We release full preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts to support community follow‑up under more challenging and diverse conditions.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/verifier‑diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and low power to detect small absolute improvements relative to the preregistered target (10 percentage points).
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot (n=60) intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not executed; the main N=300 was used as pre‑specified.
Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit when independent LLM draws per condition differ.

Representative repair transcript availability: the archived run bundle contains the low‑level repair provider trace documenting the single automated repair and subsequent validation pass (recorded in the execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation artifacts). That verbatim trace is not included in the representative manuscript excerpt; instead we report the archive‑traceable semantic summary of the repair action in Results and make the full trace available in the published artifact bundle for inspection.
